title: Construction and density of the roots

clauses.source_clause: First item: finite half-filled real roots
clauses.scope: Global finite roots exist uniquely for every real site array and pi/2 <= lambda < pi; the proof in fact covers every 2*n <= L.
The counting derivative is positive on the entire real line in the negative-kernel regime, including the actual constructed roots.

clauses.source_clause: First item: uniform density and integrated discrepancy
clauses.scope: The complete first item is proved with constants fixed before every chain length and real site array in the negative-kernel regime: finite distinct zero-twist roots, positive counting density, uniform rho_L-p_L, and ordinary half-line integrated discrepancy. Here p_L is exactly the sum of translates of the inverse-defined r; the hyperbolic formula for that same r is now proved for every physical lambda. The actual dressed source has mass L/2 and a checked cumulative primitive. The actual inverse-defined density equation is complexified and Fourier transformed using proved L1 integrability and the convolution theorem, with exact conversion between angular and Mathlib frequency conventions. Hyperbolic algebra and proved nonvanishing give its actual transform 1/(2*cosh(lambda*p/2)). The displayed profile has the same transform, is continuous and integrable, and its transform is integrable. Fourier inversion proves pointwise fullLineDensityFunction(lambda,u)=1/(2*lambda*cosh(u/(lambda/pi))) for every 0<lambda<pi and every real u.

clauses.source_clause: Second item: r_Q and H_Q comparison, mass and defect
clauses.scope: For every 0<lambda<pi,the actual inverse-defined finite-window functions satisfy c*r<=r_Q<=C*r and c<=H_Q<=C uniformly for every Q>=0 and abs(u)<=Q,including endpoints. Combining the two signs of K and the free point, the actual M_Q is strictly increasing on Q>=0, M_0=0, 0<M_Q<1/2 for every finite Q>0, and M_Q tends to1/2. Every prescribed filling rho in(0,1/2) has exactly one actual nonnegative cutoff; every family of masses converging strictly below one half has eventually bounded cutoffs. All statements hold for every 0<lambda<pi. The actual full-line exterior mass is between exp(-Q/(lambda/pi))/pi and twice that expression for Q>=0, by the identified density, evenness and actual exponential integration. The ordinary finite-window deficit is comparable to that exterior mass in both parameter regimes. Consequently the exact manuscript rate c*exp(-Q/(lambda/pi))<=1/2-M_Q<=C*exp(-Q/(lambda/pi)) is proved for every 0<lambda<pi, with positive constants chosen before every cutoff, including the free point. The positive-K proof uses the proved actual resolvent factorization and positivity;strict filling monotonicity uses actual exterior integrals rather than an assumed endpoint derivative.

clauses.source_clause: Second item: quantile stability and counting-density approximation
clauses.scope: For every physical lambda,the actual reference mid-quantiles and exact ordered roots exist at sufficiently large bounded cutoffs or under the manuscript positive-power boundary-density criterion. Weighted quantile displacement is uniformly bounded. The actual counting derivative differs from L*r_Q by O(1) on the whole line;the actual counting function differs from L times the actual cumulative density minus n/2 by O(1),including both continuum endpoints. The actual mass-selected n/L regular-filling family and the positive-power lower-bound family are assembled,with constants preceding all finite data. Actual finite mass data construct their own reference mid-quantiles and nonsingular ordered roots. Every family whose boundary density times chain length diverges has eventual actual roots with uniform weighted displacement and counting-density error. The bounded-cutoff alternative is uniform over all sufficiently large chains. The explicit c*L^a boundary lower bound with c,a positive implies the dense-boundary criterion. At every limiting filling below half,actual cutoff boundedness is derived from the finite-window mass limit,and the resulting n/L family has eventual roots. These results cover every physical lambda and use the actual manuscript density and finite equations. The actual scattering phase derivative and absolute-kernel comparison prove relative phase increments for both kernel signs. Actual weighted root closeness then gives a whole-line counting-phase displacement bound. Combined with actual reference quadrature,this proves uniform discrepancy from the actual finite-window cumulative density,including bounded counting extensions at both endpoints. A single actual-root assembler supplies ordered roots,weighted displacement,whole-line density and primitive errors,and the actual nonsingular Gaudin matrix with all constants chosen before the finite data.

clauses.source_clause: Third item: quadrature and local mass
clauses.scope: Actual inverse-density measure mass is uniformly bounded on every prescribed fixed-length moving interval. A compact-test bound from that actual interval mass controls the finite low-density range. Combining it with the previously proved large-density estimate removes the finite lower cutoff:the actual-measure bounded-Lipschitz error is C/N times(Lip(phi)+norm(phi)) for every N>0,with actual local counting density and explicit occupied-reference-window support. PhysicalRootMeasureData records genuine properties of one actual root list:ConsecutiveRoots,weighted quantile displacement,whole-line density error,original Gaudin determinant nonzero,positive actual atom weights,uniform actual unit-interval mass,a real-analytic twist branch with exact Gaudin response,and the all-positive-N actual quadrature bound. Its witnesses are constructed from the previously proved actual root,inverse and measure estimates;none of its fields is introduced as an external assumption. A single larger fixed density threshold guarantees all fields for the same X. The manuscript boundary-density criterion and actual finite mass data then construct the reference quantiles and this same actual X. The joint construction gives actual root-measure families under the dense-boundary criterion. A stronger selection theorem chooses the reference and actual roots once,before every test-window length and enlargement. For every fixed length and positive enlargement,uniform eventual measure,quadrature and analytic-branch conclusions hold for those same chosen roots. The corresponding filtered local convergence to Lebesgue measure is proved for their actual atomic measures,with varying finite root counts. The earlier regular-filling and positive-power boundary criteria supply the density hypothesis. The prior negative-K half-filled and real-array estimates remain checked. The analytic homogeneous block is complete with the explicit occupied-region and compact-support conditions. U09 remains open about the intended statement scope;the whole named lemma is not counted complete.
The connected hopping graph, free-fermion sector minimum and continuation of the Perron identification have not been formalized.

clauses.source_clause: Final paragraph: nonsingularity and analytic twist branch
clauses.scope: Negative-K actual finite roots,including all real arrays and half filling,have nonsingular Gaudin matrices and analytic twist branches by the earlier finite positivity proof. The actual all-physical homogeneous roots in the regular-filling and dense-boundary regimes now have nonsingular original Gaudin matrices by the proved nonlinear perturbation estimate. Their analytic twist branches preserve the actual equations and order near zero,and obey the actual Gaudin derivative identity. A convergent Neumann correction of the actual reference right inverse proves nonsingularity of the original actual Gaudin matrix throughout a sufficiently small weighted configuration neighborhood. The actual ordered roots and uniform density error are assembled with this nonsingularity for every physical lambda. Under the manuscript boundary-density criterion,these actual roots have real-analytic twist branches and the exact Gaudin response identity at every sufficiently nearby twist. No determinant premise or inverse is assumed for the constructed roots.
